lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 6, Session 1
lesson.footer: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 1

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 5 (VC2M5N06, VC2M5N07) with Year 6 fraction-decimal connections: writing fractions as decimals through equivalent fractions with denominators of 10, 100 and 1000, using multiplication facts
plan.shape: example-first: tenths and hundredths on a hundred grid, then making the denominator 10, 100 or 1000, because place value carries the meaning
plan.criticalFeature: make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000, then read the decimal from place value
decisionPoints: the choice check: which decimal equals 4/100?
plan.anchor: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: one amount, three names: fraction, decimal, percentage; make it out of 100 to switch
A place value chart: ones . tenths hundredths thousandths

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Hundred grids, a fraction-to-decimal table, equivalent fractions, a mistake and sport statistics.
resources.title: Fractions as Decimals
resources.subtitle: Make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000, then read the decimal.

items.prompt: Write each fraction as a decimal.

steps: 4 × 25 = 100, so multiply top and bottom by 25.

items.prompt: Write each fraction as a decimal. Make the denominator 10 or 100 first.
Sam wrote 3/4 as a decimal. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: He wrote the digits side by side. 3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75.

example.prompt: A goal shooter scored 9 of 10 shots. Decimal?

items.prompt: A netballer scored 17 of her 20 shots. Write this as a decimal.
A cricket team won 19 of its 25 games. Write this as a decimal.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Thousandths, eighths and a decimal puzzle, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Thousandths and Beyond
resources.subtitle: Make the denominator 1000.

example.prompt: Can 1/3 be made into tenths or hundredths?
steps: No whole number times 3 makes 10, 100 or 1000.
1/3 does not make a short decimal: 0.333...

items.prompt: Sort the fractions: can the denominator become 10, 100 or 1000?
Look at the denominators that work. What do you notice about their factors?
items.answer: They only have the factors 2 and 5 (like 10 = 2 × 5).

example.prompt: I am a fraction with denominator 20 and I equal 0.45. What am I?

items.prompt: Make three fraction puzzles like the example for a partner: one with denominator 4, one with 25 and one with 50. Write the answers on the back.
items.answer: Check each puzzle: the decimal matches the fraction (for example 0.75 = 3/4, 0.12 = 3/25, 0.18 = 9/50).

steps: Tenths go straight after the point: 0.4.

items.prompt: Write 1/2 as a decimal. Make it out of 10 first.

slides.notes: Session 1 of our fractions, decimals and percentages week: today we write fractions as decimals.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and draw a place value chart on the board. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Perimeter
prompts: What is the perimeter of a 14 m by 9 m rectangle?

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's area and perimeter.
ASK: What is the perimeter of a 14 metre by 9 metre rectangle?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 46 m
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> add a length and a width, then double. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 14 and 9 make 23, doubled is 46 metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 126, the area.
Fix: say perimeter goes around the edge, and they add.
notes.prep: Review of Week 5 area and perimeter (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Missing side
prompts: Area 84 m², one side 7 m. How long is the other side?

beats: ASK: How long is the other side?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12 m
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> say 7 times what is 84, and count up in sevens. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 84 divided by 7 is 12 metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 77, by subtracting.
Fix: say 7 times what makes 84, and they divide.

beats: ASK: What is the probability of red?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/8
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> count all the equal parts, then the red parts. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Red is 3 of 8 equal parts, so 3/8. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 3/5, red out of the others.
Fix: count all 8 parts for the bottom number, and they rewrite it.

beats: SAY: Now for our eight times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 8 times 7?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 56
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double, double, double: 14, 28, 56. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 56. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 54 or 63.
Fix: double 7 three times: 14, 28, 56, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's the next one.
ASK: What is 8 times 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 72
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 8 tens is 80, take one 8 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 72. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 81.
Fix: 8 tens is 80, take away 8, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many eights make 64?
ASK: What is 64 divided by 8?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 8
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> halve 64 three times: 32, 16, 8. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 8. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 7 or 9.
Fix: check: 8 eights is 64, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to write fractions as decimals using tenths, hundredths and thousandths.
successCriteria: I can write tenths and hundredths as decimals.
I can make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000 to write a fraction as a decimal.
I can explain how place value shows the fraction in a decimal.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week, every amount has three names: a fraction, a decimal and a percentage.
Today we turn fractions into decimals.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 tenths and hundredths is reachable for everyone; SC2 making the denominator 10, 100 or 1000 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 place value is the stretch.

slides.title: Name the shaded part
slides.prompt: What fraction is shaded? Write it as a decimal too.

beats: POINT to the grid.
SAY: This grid has 100 equal squares.
Some of you may remember shading grids like this.
ASK: What fraction is shaded, and how would you write it as a decimal?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 30/100 or 3/10, and 0.3
SCAN boards for 0.3.
80%+ -> cold call one student: Why 0.3 and not 0.03?
Less -> count the shaded rows: 3 rows of 10, 3 tenths. Re-ask.
SAY: It's 30 hundredths, which is 3 tenths, or 0.3.
One amount, different names. That's our week.
trap: writing 0.03.
Fix: count the full rows as tenths, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: a hundred grid shows both names. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A number that uses a decimal point to show parts of a whole: tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is decimal. Say it with me: dec-i-mal.
SAY: After the decimal point come tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths.
Each place is ten times smaller than the one before.
ASK: In 0.75, which digit shows the hundredths?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 5
trap: saying 7.
Fix: point along the chart: tenths, then hundredths, and they look again.
notes.prep: Place value carries the meaning; keep the chart on the board.

beats: POINT to the shaded squares.
SAY: 23 squares out of 100 are shaded. That's 23 hundredths.
MODEL the place value chart.
SAY: 23 hundredths is 2 tenths and 3 hundredths,
so I write 0, point, 2 in the tenths, 3 in the hundredths: 0.23.
ASK: How would you write 9 hundredths as a decimal?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.09
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 0.09. Zero tenths, 9 hundredths.
The zero holds the tenths place.
trap: writing 0.9.
Fix: say 9 hundredths has no full tenths, and they rewrite it.
notes.help: Write the digits into a place value chart first.
notes.prep: Hundredths sit two places after the point. SC1.

beats: POINT to the quarters.
SAY: To write 3/4 as a decimal, I want hundredths.
4 times 25 is 100, so each quarter is 25 hundredths.
MODEL multiplying top and bottom by 25.
SAY: Three quarters is 75 hundredths, which is 0.75.
ASK: Now you try: how would you write 7/20 as a decimal?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.35
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 times 5 is 100, so 7/20 is 35 hundredths: 0.35.
trap: writing 0.720 or 7.20.
Fix: ask what times 20 makes 100, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Write 3/8 as a decimal using thousandths.
notes.help: List the times table of the denominator up to 100.
notes.prep: The critical feature: make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000 first. SC2.

slides.title: Which decimal equals 4/100?
slides.prompt: Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: writes the numerator and denominator side by side

beats: SAY: Think about which place the 4 belongs in.
ASK: Which decimal equals 4 hundredths?
10 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What is A as a fraction?
Less -> write 4 into the hundredths column of the chart. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 0.04: zero tenths and 4 hundredths.
A is 4 tenths, and C is not a decimal of 4/100 at all.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: shade 4 squares on a hundred grid, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A: hundredths read as tenths; C: digits side by side.

slides.title: Write it as a decimal
slides.ask: Write the fraction as a decimal.
slides.pivot: make the denominator 10 or 100 on the board together
slides.followUp: cold call one board: What did you multiply by?

say: Write each decimal on your board.
trap: dropping the zero in 0.06.
Fix: write it into the place value chart, and they fix it.
notes.stretch: Write each one as a percentage too.
notes.help: Use the place value chart on the board.
notes.prep: Guided practice: tenths, hundredths, a zero place holder, equivalents and thousandths. SC1 and SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Make the denominator 100 first.
ASK: How do you write 13/20 as a decimal?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.65
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> ask what times 20 makes 100, then multiply the top. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 times 5 is 100, and 13 times 5 is 65: 0.65.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 0.13.
Fix: say twentieths are not hundredths yet, and they multiply.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone writing 0.1320 or 1.3 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Write fractions as decimals on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: What did you make the denominator?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: writing the digits side by side.
Fix: make the denominator 100 first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: thousandths, fractions that will not work, and a puzzle.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: hundred grids to read and a place value frame.
notes.prep: Independent practice: grids, a fraction table, equivalents, a mistake and sport statistics. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: How do you write 11/25 as a decimal?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 0.44
RECORD who writes 0.1125 or 0.11.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing 0.11.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: twenty-fifths, a new denominator.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you turn a fraction into a decimal.

notes.answer: open - listen for make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000, then read it
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can write a fraction as a decimal?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 0.11 on the board matters most.
ASK: How do you turn a fraction into a decimal?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000, then read it
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: fractions as division.
